152/* The splitmix64 output function: a bijective 64-bit hash */
153static inline uint64_t mix64(uint64_t z) {
154 z = (z ^ (z >> 30)) * 0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9ULL;
155 z = (z ^ (z >> 27)) * 0x94d049bb133111ebULL;
156 return z ^ (z >> 31);
157}
158
159static inline uint64_t splitmix64(uint64_t *state) {
160 return mix64(*state += 0x9e3779b97f4a7c15ULL);
161}
162
163static inline int rand_uniform_thread(int max, uint64_t *state) {
164 if (max <= 1) return 0;
165 return (int)(splitmix64(state) % (uint64_t)max);
166}
167
168static inline mzp_t * mzp_rand_thread(mzp_t *q, rci_t length, uint64_t *state) {
169 if (q == NULL) return NULL;
170 for (int i = 0; i <= (int)length - 2; i++) {
171 q->values[i] = i + rand_uniform_thread(length - i, state);
172 }
173 for (int i = length - 1; i < (int)q->length; i++) {
174 q->values[i] = i;
175 }
176 return q;
177}

179#define CC_SPLIT_MAX_LEVELS 3 /* CC work units: at most 3 fixed levels, B^3 units per start index (cc_round_levels()) */

181/* The CC column-syndrome hash, for the last two levels of a cluster (see cc_walk_last2()). The hash of a set S of rows
182 * of H is the XOR of the random 64-bit values zr[r], r in S (Zobrist hashing): the hash of the syndrome s + h_c, where
183 * h_c is the column c of H, is that of s XOR hc[c]. The nonzero columns are sorted by (hash, column), and each
184 * distinct hash value `key` has an entry {key, beg, cnt} in the open-addressing table `tab` (linear probing from the
185 * slot key >> tshift) for its run of columns cols[beg..beg+cnt-1]. The bit (key & bmask) of the filter `bits` is set
186 * for each key, so that most failed lookups only read one bit. */
187typedef struct {
188 uint64_t key;
189 int beg, cnt; /* cnt = 0: empty slot */
190} cc_hash_slot_t;
191
192typedef struct {
193 uint64_t *zr; /* random value of each row of H */
194 uint64_t *hc; /* hash of each column of H (0 for a zero column) */
195 uint64_t *bits; /* filter: bit (key & bmask) set for each key */
196 uint64_t bmask;
197 cc_hash_slot_t *tab; /* 2^(64-tshift) slots */
198 int tshift;
199 int tmask;
200 int *cols; /* the nonzero columns sorted by (hash, column) */
201 int ncols; /* their number */
202 int nkeys; /* number of distinct keys */
203} cc_hash_t;

323/* Reasons why the run ended (the first one recorded, see ctx_stop()), reported with DBG_SUMMARY */
324enum {
325 STOP_NONE = 0,
326 STOP_BOUNDS, /* the bounds coincide: dmin = dmax */
327 STOP_CC_FOUND, /* CC found a codeword (the exact distance, unless lower weights were not scanned) */
328 STOP_RW_CONVERGED, /* method 1: RW `min_hits` convergence */
329 STOP_RW_STEPS, /* method 1: all RW steps done */
330 STOP_TIMEOUT, /* timeout reached */
331 STOP_CC_DONE, /* CC done up to the largest weight needed (wmax), and RW ended */
332 STOP_CC_SLOW, /* method 3: the next CC round is predicted not to finish before the timeout, and RW ended */
333 STOP_WMIN, /* a codeword of weight <= wmin found */
334 STOP_MAXC, /* maxC codewords collected */
335 STOP_COLLECTED, /* the CC rounds w = d..d+dW enumerated all codewords to collect (outC, maxC) */
336 STOP_DSTOP, /* the lower bound reached the stop target: dmin >= dstop */
337 STOP_K0 /* the rank check found k = 0: no codeword (see k0_check_start()) */
338};

340/* Stop all threads, recording the `reason` unless one is already recorded */
341static inline void ctx_stop(distfork_ctx_t * const ctx, const int reason) {
342 int none = STOP_NONE;
343 atomic_compare_exchange_strong(&ctx->stop_reason, &none, reason);
344 atomic_store(&ctx->stop_flag, true);
345}
346
347/* The target t of the CC rounds: the upper bound dmax, or the stop target dstop if smaller (0: neither). The rounds
348 * w <= t-1 certify dmin = t (with outC, the rounds w = t..t+dW collect codewords). Unlike dmax, dstop is not an upper
349 * bound: once dmin >= dstop, the run ends with the bounds [dmin, dmax] (dmax = 0 if no codeword was found). */
350static inline int ctx_target(const distfork_ctx_t * const ctx, const int cur_dmax) {
351 const int dstop = ctx->p->dstop;
352 return (dstop > 0 && (cur_dmax == 0 || dstop < cur_dmax)) ? dstop : cur_dmax;
353}

355/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- *
356 * Opt-in time stamps (`stamp=1`) and JSON result summary (`json=1|FILE`, schema "dm4ri-result/1"). When neither
357 * option is active, all helpers are no-ops and the default output is unchanged.
358 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
359typedef struct {
360 char s[32];
361} tstamp_t;
362
363static inline tstamp_t tstamp_at(const params_t * const p, double t) {
364 tstamp_t ts;
365 if (!p->stamp) {
366 ts.s[0] = '\0';
367 return ts;
368 }
369 if (!(t >= 0.0)) t = 0.0;
370 snprintf(ts.s, sizeof(ts.s), " [t=%.3fs]", t);
371 return ts;
372}
373
374static inline tstamp_t tstamp_now(const distfork_ctx_t * const ctx) {
375 if (!ctx->p->stamp) {
376 tstamp_t ts;
377 ts.s[0] = '\0';
378 return ts;
379 }
380 return tstamp_at(ctx->p, get_time_sec() - ctx->start_time);
381}

466static void res_event_push_locked(const double t, const int lb, const int ub) {
467 if (res.nev > 0 && res.ev[res.nev - 1].lb == lb && res.ev[res.nev - 1].ub == ub) return;
468 if (res.nev == res.ev_cap) {
469 res.ev_cap = res.ev_cap ? res.ev_cap * 2 : 32;
470 res.ev = realloc(res.ev, (size_t)res.ev_cap * sizeof(res_ev_t));
471 if (!res.ev) ERROR("memory allocation");
472 }
473 double tt = (t >= 0.0 && isfinite(t)) ? t : 0.0;
474 if (res.nev > 0 && tt < res.ev[res.nev - 1].t) tt = res.ev[res.nev - 1].t;
475 res.ev[res.nev++] = (res_ev_t){.t = tt, .lb = lb, .ub = ub};
476}
477
478static void res_event_push(const double t, const int lb, const int ub) {
479 if (!res.on) return;
480 pthread_mutex_lock(&res.ev_mtx);
481 res_event_push_locked(t, lb, ub);
482 pthread_mutex_unlock(&res.ev_mtx);
483}

485static void res_event_ctx_at(const distfork_ctx_t * const ctx, const double t) {
486 if (!res.on) return;
487 pthread_mutex_lock(&res.ev_mtx);
488 res_event_push_locked(t, atomic_load(&ctx->dmin), atomic_load(&ctx->dmax));
489 pthread_mutex_unlock(&res.ev_mtx);
490}

509static void res_witness_set(const int * const cols, const int w, const char * const src) {
510 if (!res.on || w <= 0 || !cols) return;
511 if (res.wit_w > 0 && w >= res.wit_w) return;

514 if (!res.wit_cols) ERROR("memory allocation");
515 res.wit_cap = w;
516 }

518 res.wit_w = w;
519 res.wit_src = src;
520}

522static void res_witness_from_hash(const params_t * const p, const char * const src) {
523 if (!res.on || p->min_w == INT_MAX) return;
524 if (res.wit_w > 0 && p->min_w >= res.wit_w) return;
525 for (const cw_vec_t *cw = p->codewords; cw != NULL; cw = (const cw_vec_t *)(cw->hh.next)) {
526 if (cw->weight == p->min_w) {
527 res_witness_set(cw->arr, cw->weight, src);
528 return;
529 }
530 }
531}

544/* A CC round at weight w hands out the work units u = beg*R .. (end+1)*R-1 one at a time, where beg..end are the start
545 * indices of the round (see cc_round_beg(), cc_round_end()) and R = B^L (see cc_round_levels()). The unit u = i*R + k
546 * grows the clusters from the start index i = u / R, with the branches of the first L levels fixed by the digits
547 * k_0, k_1, ... of k = k_0 + k_1*B + ... in radix B, the maximum row weight of H: at level l = 1..L (a cluster of l
548 * columns), start_CC_recurs_mt() only adds the column at position k_{l-1} of the row it extends (none if the row is
549 * shorter: an empty unit). The units of a start index explore together the same clusters as the start index itself
550 * (L = 0), in pieces small enough to balance the load if there are few start indices per thread (the clusters from the
551 * first start column, which only grow to larger columns, are about w/n of the round). The weight, the number of fixed
552 * levels L, and the next unit are packed into the single atomic word `cc_next`, so that a worker always processes a
553 * claimed unit with the parameters of its round, even if it joins just as the coordinator publishes the next round. */
554#define CC_IDX_BITS 32
555#define CC_LEV_SHIFT 48
556static inline long long cc_pack(const int w, const int lev, const int idx) {
557 return ((long long)lev << CC_LEV_SHIFT) | ((long long)w << CC_IDX_BITS) | (long long)(unsigned int)idx;
558}
559static inline int cc_unpack_w(const long long v) { return (int)((v >> CC_IDX_BITS) & 0xffff); }
560static inline int cc_unpack_lev(const long long v) { return (int)((v >> CC_LEV_SHIFT) & 0xf); }
561static inline int cc_unpack_idx(const long long v) { return (int)(v & 0xffffffffLL); }
562
563/* First start index of a CC round: index into the expert `start` list, or the first start column (cbeg) */
564static inline int cc_round_beg(const params_t * const p) {
565 return (p->start_num > 0) ? 0 : ((p->cbeg >= 0) ? p->cbeg : 0);
566}
567
568/* Last start index of a CC round at weight w: a cluster started at column i only uses columns > i, so it
569 * starts at column n-w at the latest (expert `start` list: all listed columns, clusters are unlimited) */
570static inline int cc_round_end(const params_t * const p, const int w) {
571 if (p->start_num > 0) return p->start_num - 1;
572 const int nvar = p->spaH->cols;
573 return (p->cend >= 0) ? minint(p->cend, nvar - w) : (nvar - w);
574}
575
576/* Last work unit of the CC round at weight w with `lev` fixed levels (in range, see cc_round_levels()) */
577static inline int cc_unit_last(const distfork_ctx_t * const ctx, const int w, const int lev) {
578 return (cc_round_end(ctx->p, w) + 1) * ctx->cc_R[lev] - 1;
579}
580
581#define CC_SPLIT_UNITS_PER_THREAD 4.0 /* aim at >= 4 work units of the size of the largest one per CC thread */
582#define CC_SPLIT_MIN_WORK 1e-3 /* rounds predicted to take < 1 ms on all threads (on the start indices of an
583 * expert `start` list, if they are fewer): whole start indices */
584#define CC_SPLIT_CLAIMS_PER_WORK 1e4 /* at most 10^4 work units per thread-second of predicted work */
585#define CC_SPLIT_CLAIMS_UNKNOWN 65536 /* at most this many work units if the work of the round is not known */
586
587/* Number of fixed levels L of the work units of the CC round at weight w over the start indices beg..end, with the
588 * estimated work `est` (thread-seconds, 0 if not known, see cc_work_estimate()), see `cc_pack()`: the smallest L which
589 * gives CC_SPLIT_UNITS_PER_THREAD units per thread, where the largest unit is taken as the unit size: whole start
590 * indices count as n/w units (the clusters from the first start column are about w/n of the round; the columns of the
591 * expert `start` list are alike, with unlimited clusters), and each fixed level divides the units by the typical
592 * number of branches. L = 0 for short rounds (with a short `start` list, only if they are short on its start indices,
593 * which are then all that can work in parallel), and L <= min(3, w-3), so that at least two levels of a unit are free.
594 * The number of units (each one claim of the shared counter, empty units included) is limited by the predicted work,
595 * and all units must have an index < INT_MAX - num_threads (over-claims at the end of the round). */
596static int cc_round_levels(const distfork_ctx_t * const ctx, const int w, const int beg, const int end,
597 const double est) {
598 const int nthr = ctx->num_threads;
599 const int n_start = end - beg + 1;
600 const int lmax = minint(CC_SPLIT_MAX_LEVELS, w - 3);
601 if (nthr <= 1 || n_start <= 0 || lmax <= 0 || ctx->cc_B <= 1) return 0;
602 const int busy = (ctx->p->start_num > 0) ? minint(nthr, n_start) : nthr; /* threads busy with whole start indices */
603 if (est > 0.0 && est < CC_SPLIT_MIN_WORK * busy) return 0;
604 const double max_units = (est > 0.0) ? CC_SPLIT_CLAIMS_PER_WORK * est : CC_SPLIT_CLAIMS_UNKNOWN;
605 double units = (ctx->p->start_num > 0) ? (double)n_start : (double)n_start / w;
606 int lev = 0;
607 while (lev < lmax && units < CC_SPLIT_UNITS_PER_THREAD * nthr) {
608 const long long R = ctx->cc_R[lev + 1];
609 if (R <= 0 || (double)n_start * (double)R > max_units || ((long long)end + 1) * R > (long long)INT_MAX - nthr - 1)
610 break;
611 lev++;
612 units *= ctx->cc_branch;
613 }
614 return lev;
615}
616
617/* Update the RW weight limit for the `min_hits` statistic after a change of the codeword hash (under `cw_mutex`). It
618 * is stored only if changed, as it shares the cache line of the bounds, which RW threads read for every candidate. */
619static inline void ctx_update_feed_limit(distfork_ctx_t * const ctx) {
620 const int feed = codeword_feed_limit(ctx->p);
621 if (atomic_load_explicit(&ctx->cw_feed_limit, memory_order_relaxed) != feed) {
622 atomic_store_explicit(&ctx->cw_feed_limit, feed, memory_order_relaxed);
623 }
624}
625
626/* irred=1: is the codeword of the `cnt` columns `vec` irreducible, i.e., not the union of a codeword and a disjoint
627 * nonzero zero-syndrome vector? Iff the rank of its columns of H is cnt - 1 (see csr_cols_rank()). Always true with
628 * irred=0. */
629static inline bool cw_irreducible(const distfork_ctx_t * const ctx, cols_ws_t * const ws, const int cnt,
630 const int vec[]) {
631 if (!ctx->p->irred || !ws || cnt < 2) return true;
632 return csr_cols_rank(ctx->mHT_cc, cnt, vec, ws) == cnt - 1;
633}
634
635/* Stage 5 (under `cw_mutex`): the table of the canonical classes follows the minimum weight min_w of the codewords in
636 * hash (the classes of a heavier weight are removed once a lighter codeword is recorded) */
637static void rw_canon_sync_locked(distfork_ctx_t * const ctx) {
638 params_t * const p = ctx->p;
639 if (!ctx->canon_tab || p->min_w >= p->canon.w) return;
640 rw_canon_tab_clear(ctx->canon_tab);
641 rw_canon_stats_t * const cs = &p->canon;
642 cs->w = p->min_w;
643 cs->classes = cs->raw = cs->n_unif = cs->f1 = cs->f2 = 0;
644 cs->full = 0;
645 atomic_store_explicit(&ctx->canon_w, p->min_w, memory_order_relaxed);
646}
647
648/* Record the CC codeword `err` (sorted columns, nonzero syndrome of L) found by worker `warg`, and update the upper
649 * bound; returns true if the run is to stop (the first codeword without outC and maxC, or maxC codewords). With
650 * irred=1, a reducible codeword is not recorded (counted in `cw_red_cc`); the CC search finds every irreducible
651 * codeword, but only some reducible ones, from the weight d + 3 on for a circuit DEM (doc/cc_completeness.tex). */
652static __attribute__((noinline)) bool cc_record(distfork_ctx_t * const ctx, const worker_arg_t * const warg,
653 const one_vec_t * const err) {
654 params_t * const p = ctx->p;
655 if (!cw_irreducible(ctx, warg->irr_ws, err->wei, err->vec)) {
656 atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&ctx->cw_red_cc, 1, memory_order_relaxed);
657 return false;
658 }
659 bool stop = false;
660 pthread_mutex_lock(&ctx->cw_mutex);
661 p->codewords = codeword_add_maybe(p, err->vec, err->wei, CW_SRC_OTHER);
662 if (res.on && err->wei == p->min_w) res_witness_set(err->vec, err->wei, "cc");
663 ctx_update_feed_limit(ctx);
664 rw_canon_sync_locked(ctx);
665 int cur_d = atomic_load(&ctx->dmax);
666 if (p->min_w < cur_d || cur_d == 0) {
667 atomic_store(&ctx->dmax, p->min_w);
668 res_event_ctx(ctx);
669 if ((p->debug & DBG_CODEWORDS) && err->wei == p->min_w) {
670 char prefix[48];
671 snprintf(prefix, sizeof(prefix), "# [thread %d] CC codeword", warg->tid);
672 print_codeword_support(stderr, prefix, err->vec, err->wei, p->debug);
673 }
674 }
675 int cur_cc_found = atomic_load(&ctx->cc_found_weight);
676 if (cur_cc_found == 0 || err->wei < cur_cc_found) {
677 atomic_store(&ctx->cc_found_weight, err->wei);
678 }
679 if (!p->outC && p->maxC == 0) {
680 ctx_stop(ctx, STOP_CC_FOUND);
681 stop = true;
682 }
683 if (codeword_maxc_reached(p)) {
684 ctx_stop(ctx, STOP_MAXC);
685 stop = true;
686 }
687 pthread_mutex_unlock(&ctx->cw_mutex);
688 return stop;
689}
690
691static inline int bit_get(const uint64_t * const b, const int i) { return (int)((b[i >> 6] >> (i & 63)) & 1); }
692static inline void bit_flip(uint64_t * const b, const int i) { b[i >> 6] ^= (uint64_t)1 << (i & 63); }
693
694/* The first set bit of the bitset b in from..limit-1 (limit if none) */
695static inline int bits_first(const uint64_t * const b, const int from, const int limit) {
696 if (from >= limit) return limit;
697 int k = from >> 6;
698 const int k_last = (limit - 1) >> 6;
699 uint64_t x = b[k] & (~(uint64_t)0 << (from & 63));
700 while (x == 0) {
701 if (++k > k_last) return limit;
702 x = b[k];
703 }
704 const int r = (k << 6) + __builtin_ctzll(x);
705 return (r < limit) ? r : limit;
706}
707
708/* The state of the CC walk of a worker (smax = 0, see cc_walk() and, for cc_prune >= 1, cc_bnb()) */
709typedef struct {
710 distfork_ctx_t *ctx;
711 worker_arg_t *warg;
712 const csr_t *mH; /* H (sorted rows) */
713 const csr_t *mHT; /* its transpose: the columns of H (sorted rows) */
714 const cc_hash_t *hs; /* the column-syndrome hash */
715 uint64_t *S; /* the syndrome of the cluster: bitset of the rows of H */
716 uint64_t *E; /* the columns of the cluster: bitset */
717 int *cols; /* the columns of the cluster in the order added (cols[0]: the start column) */
718 one_vec_t *cw; /* a codeword found: its sorted columns */
719 int w; /* the number of columns of the cluster */
720 int col_min; /* columns are added only if larger (-1: unlimited clusters with the expert `start` list) */
721 int w_limit; /* the weight of the CC round */
722 int max_col_wt; /* the maximum column weight of H */
723 int m; /* the number of rows of H */
724 const int *fix; /* the fixed levels 1..nfix of the work unit, see `cc_pack()` */
725 int nfix;
726 long long nodes; /* calls of the recursion (cc_walk() or cc_bnb()), added to ctx->cc_nodes after each round */
727 int count_w; /* the nodes of weight w >= count_w are counted: a node at a fixed level is visited by all the
728 * work units with the same earlier digits, and counted in the one whose later digits are 0 */
729 /* the branch and bound (cc_prune >= 1, see cc_bnb()): a column u is available if u > col_min and u is neither in
730 * the cluster S nor in the forbidden set F */
731 int prune; /* cc_prune: 1, or 2 with the coverage and fractional cover bounds */
732 int max_row_wt; /* the maximum row weight of H (at most this many branches per node) */
733 uint64_t *X; /* the columns of S and F: bitset */
734 int *acnt; /* the number of available columns of each row of H */
735 int acnt_col; /* the value of col_min for which acnt is set up (INT_MIN: not set up) */
736 int *kfirst; /* the position in mH of the first column u > col_min of each row (the columns of a row are
737 * sorted, so that the loops over the available columns of a row start there) */
738 int *fstk; /* the forbidden columns in the order forbidden (unwound when the node returns) */
739 int fsp; /* their number */
740 int *brl; /* the branches of the nodes: max_row_wt entries per depth */
741 int *ulist; /* the unsatisfied rows of the current node */
742 int *uacnt; /* their numbers of available columns (acnt), for the packing bound */
743 int *ord; /* the unsatisfied rows ordered by their available columns, for the packing bound */
744 int *bcnt; /* counts of the rows by their available columns (max_row_wt + 2 entries) */
745 uint32_t *mark; /* columns marked in generation `gen` (packing and coverage bounds) */
746 uint32_t gen;
747 int *cv; /* cc_prune=2: the unsatisfied rows of each available column (generation `gen`) */
748 int *touched; /* cc_prune=2: the available columns of the unsatisfied rows */
749 int *hist; /* cc_prune=2: histogram of cv (max_col_wt + 1 entries) */
750} cc_walk_t;
751
752/* Record the codeword: the cluster with the columns c1 (unless negative) and c2, if its syndrome of L is nonzero;
753 * returns true if the run is to stop */
754static bool cc_walk_found(cc_walk_t * const t, const int c1, const int c2) {
755 one_vec_t * const cw = t->cw;
756 int n = 0;
757 for (int i = 0; i < t->w; i++) cw->vec[n++] = t->cols[i];
758 if (c1 >= 0) cw->vec[n++] = c1;
759 cw->vec[n++] = c2;
760 for (int i = 1; i < n; i++) { /* insertion sort */
761 const int x = cw->vec[i];
762 int j = i - 1;
763 while (j >= 0 && cw->vec[j] > x) {
764 cw->vec[j + 1] = cw->vec[j];
765 j--;
766 }
767 cw->vec[j + 1] = x;
768 }
769 cw->wei = n;
770 const colmask_t * const mL = t->ctx->p->maskL; /* NULL for a classical code */
771 if (mL && !colmask_syndrome_non_zero(mL, n, cw->vec)) return false;
772 return cc_record(t->ctx, t->warg, cw);
773}
774
775/* Is the syndrome S (bitset of weight sw) the sum h_{c1} + h_{c2} of the columns c1 and c2 of H (rows of mHT)? */
776static bool cc_sum2_equal(const uint64_t * const S, const int sw, const csr_t * const mHT, const int c1, const int c2) {
777 int a = mHT->p[c1], b = mHT->p[c2], k = 0;
778 const int a_end = mHT->p[c1 + 1], b_end = mHT->p[c2 + 1];
779 while (a < a_end || b < b_end) {
780 int r;
781 if (b >= b_end) r = mHT->i[a++];
782 else if (a >= a_end) r = mHT->i[b++];
783 else if (mHT->i[a] < mHT->i[b]) r = mHT->i[a++];
784 else if (mHT->i[b] < mHT->i[a]) r = mHT->i[b++];
785 else { /* a common row cancels */
786 a++;
787 b++;
788 continue;
789 }
790 if (!bit_get(S, r)) return false;
791 k++;
792 }
793 return k == sw;
794}
795
796/* The last two levels of cc_walk() at the level w = t->w with w + 2 = current_limit (the leaf level w + 1 is not a
797 * fixed level of the work unit; `i1_beg`..`i1_end`: the positions in mH of the columns of the row r0 = min(S) to add).
798 * There, the recursion adds each column c1 > col_min of r0 not in the cluster with the syndrome s = S + h_{c1} nonzero,
799 * and the leaf level adds each column c2 > col_min of the row min(s) not in the cluster with h_{c2} = s, which gives a
800 * codeword. These columns c2 are found by a lookup of the hash h ^ hc[c1] of s instead (cc_hash_t, verified exactly).
801 * The pairs (c1, c2) are the same and come in the same order (c2 in ascending order, as in the row min(s)). As at the
802 * entry of the leaf level, a codeword is not recorded once the stop flag is set or the weight limit has dropped (a
803 * smaller upper bound). Returns 1 if the run is to stop. */
804static __attribute__((noinline)) int cc_walk_last2(cc_walk_t * const t, const int sw, const uint64_t h,
805 const int i1_beg, const int i1_end) {
806 distfork_ctx_t * const ctx = t->ctx;
807 const cc_hash_t * const hs = t->hs;
808 const uint64_t * const hc = hs->hc;
809 const uint64_t * const bits = hs->bits;
810 const uint64_t bmask = hs->bmask;
811 const csr_t * const mH = t->mH;
812 const int col_min = t->col_min;
813 for (int i1 = i1_beg; i1 < i1_end; i1++) {
814 const int c1 = mH->i[i1];
815 if (c1 <= col_min) continue;
816 const uint64_t key = h ^ hc[c1]; /* the hash of s = S + h_{c1} */
817 const uint64_t fb = key & bmask;
818 if (!((bits[fb >> 6] >> (fb & 63)) & 1)) continue;
819 int j = (int)(key >> hs->tshift);
820 while (hs->tab[j].cnt > 0 && hs->tab[j].key != key) j = (j + 1) & hs->tmask;
821 if (hs->tab[j].cnt == 0) continue;
822 /* columns c2 with the hash of s (s is nonzero: no zero columns in the table) */
823 if (bit_get(t->E, c1)) continue;
824 const int k_end = hs->tab[j].beg + hs->tab[j].cnt;
825 for (int k = hs->tab[j].beg; k < k_end; k++) {
826 const int c2 = hs->cols[k];
827 if (c2 <= col_min || c2 == c1 || bit_get(t->E, c2)) continue;
828 if (!cc_sum2_equal(t->S, sw, t->mHT, c1, c2)) continue; /* a hash collision */
829 /* the checks at the entry of the leaf level */
830 if (atomic_load_explicit(&ctx->stop_flag, memory_order_relaxed)) return 0;
831 const int cur_dmax = atomic_load_explicit(&ctx->dmax, memory_order_relaxed);
832 if (cur_dmax > 0 && ctx->p->dW >= 0 && minint(t->w_limit, cur_dmax + ctx->p->dW) < t->w + 2) return 0;
833 if (cc_walk_found(t, c1, c2)) return 1;
834 }
835 }
836 return 0;
837}
838
839/* The CC recursion of start_CC_recurs_mt() for smax = 0, with the syndrome of the cluster as the bitset t->S (weight
840 * sw, smallest row r0, hash h, see cc_hash_t), and its columns as the bitset t->E: a column is added by flipping its
841 * rows in S (and back after the recursion) instead of merging sorted lists, and the weight of the new syndrome is
842 * known before. The clusters are the same, in the same order, and so are the codewords found (and their CC hit
843 * counts). The last two levels use hash lookups (cc_walk_last2()). Returns 1 if the run is to stop. */
844static int cc_walk(cc_walk_t * const t, const int sw, const int r0, const uint64_t h) {
845 distfork_ctx_t * const ctx = t->ctx;
846 if (atomic_load_explicit(&ctx->stop_flag, memory_order_relaxed)) return 0;
847 const params_t * const p = ctx->p;
848 const int w = t->w;
849 int current_limit = t->w_limit;
850 const int cur_dmax = atomic_load_explicit(&ctx->dmax, memory_order_relaxed);
851 if (cur_dmax > 0 && p->dW >= 0) current_limit = minint(t->w_limit, cur_dmax + p->dW);
852 if (w >= current_limit) return 0;
853 if (w >= t->count_w) t->nodes++;
854 const csr_t * const mH = t->mH;
855 const csr_t * const mHT = t->mHT;
856 /* the positions in mH of the columns of the row r0 to add: all of them, or one at a fixed level of the work unit */
857 int i1_beg = mH->p[r0], i1_end = mH->p[r0 + 1];
858 if (w <= t->nfix) {
859 i1_beg += t->fix[w - 1];
860 if (i1_beg >= i1_end) return 0;
861 i1_end = i1_beg + 1;
862 }
863 const int col_min = t->col_min;
864 uint64_t * const S = t->S;
865 uint64_t * const E = t->E;
866
867 if (w + 1 == current_limit) { /* leaf level: the columns c with h_c = S */
868 for (int i1 = i1_beg; i1 < i1_end; i1++) {
869 const int c = mH->i[i1];
870 if (c <= col_min) continue;
871 const int pb = mHT->p[c];
872 if (mHT->p[c + 1] - pb != sw) continue;
873 int k = 0;
874 while (k < sw && bit_get(S, mHT->i[pb + k])) k++;
875 if (k < sw || bit_get(E, c)) continue;
876 if (cc_walk_found(t, -1, c)) return 1;
877 }
878 return 0;
879 }
880 if (w + 2 == current_limit && w + 1 > t->nfix) return cc_walk_last2(t, sw, h, i1_beg, i1_end);
881
882 /* internal level */
883 const int max_reach = (current_limit - (w + 1)) * t->max_col_wt;
884 const uint64_t * const hc = t->hs->hc;
885 for (int i1 = i1_beg; i1 < i1_end; i1++) {
886 const int c1 = mH->i[i1];
887 if (c1 <= col_min) continue;
888 const int pb = mHT->p[c1], pe = mHT->p[c1 + 1];
889 if (sw - (pe - pb) > max_reach || bit_get(E, c1)) continue;
890 int nset = 0; /* the rows of c1 in S */
891 for (int k = pb; k < pe; k++) nset += bit_get(S, mHT->i[k]);
892 const int sw1 = sw + (pe - pb) - 2 * nset;
893 if (sw1 <= 0 || sw1 > max_reach) continue;
894 /* add c1: flip its rows; the smallest row of the new syndrome (r0 is in c1, all the other rows of S are larger) */
895 int rmin = t->m;
896 for (int k = pb; k < pe; k++) {
897 const int r = mHT->i[k];
898 if (!bit_get(S, r) && r < rmin) rmin = r;
899 bit_flip(S, r);
900 }
901 const int r1 = (rmin < r0) ? rmin : bits_first(S, r0 + 1, rmin);
902 bit_flip(E, c1);
903 t->cols[t->w++] = c1;
904 const int result = cc_walk(t, sw1, r1, h ^ hc[c1]);
905 t->w--;
906 bit_flip(E, c1);
907 for (int k = pb; k < pe; k++) bit_flip(S, mHT->i[k]);
908 if (result == 1) return 1;
909 }
910 return 0;
911}
912
913/* The CC work unit from the start column `col` (w_limit > 1, see cc_walk()) */
914static void cc_walk_unit(cc_walk_t * const t, const int col, const int w_limit, const int * const fix, const int nfix) {
915 const csr_t * const mHT = t->mHT;
916 const int pb = mHT->p[col], pe = mHT->p[col + 1];
917 for (int k = pb; k < pe; k++) bit_flip(t->S, mHT->i[k]);
918 bit_flip(t->E, col);
919 t->cols[0] = col;
920 t->w = 1;
921 t->col_min = (t->ctx->p->start_num > 0 && !t->ctx->p->start_scan) ? -1 : col;
922 t->w_limit = w_limit;
923 t->fix = fix;
924 t->nfix = nfix;
925 t->count_w = nfix + 1; /* (see cc_walk_t: count_w - 1 = the first fixed level with only zero digits from there on) */
926 while (t->count_w > 1 && fix[t->count_w - 2] == 0) t->count_w--;
927 cc_walk(t, pe - pb, mHT->i[pb], t->hs->hc[col]);
928 t->w = 0;
929 bit_flip(t->E, col);
930 for (int k = pb; k < pe; k++) bit_flip(t->S, mHT->i[k]);
931}
932
933/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
934 * The branch-and-bound CC search (cc_prune >= 1, smax = 0; see doc/cc_completeness.tex for the proof). A node is a
935 * cluster S with a nonzero syndrome s and a forbidden set F: a column u is available if u > col_min (the start column,
936 * F_0 = {u < start column}; with the expert `start` list, the columns listed before the start column) and u is not
937 * in S or F. With R = limit - |S| columns left, a node is pruned by admissible lower bounds on the number of columns
938 * needed to complete S to a codeword: |s| > R * max_col_wt (b1, as in cc_walk()), an unsatisfied row without
939 * available columns (dead end), more than R unsatisfied rows with pairwise disjoint sets of available columns (b2,
940 * packing, found greedily; with R >= 3), and with cc_prune=2 the coverage and fractional cover bounds (with R >= 4).
941 * Otherwise it branches on the unsatisfied row with the fewest available columns (the first such row in the row
942 * order), over its available columns v_1..v_q in column order: the branch i adds v_i to S, and v_i is forbidden in the
943 * later branches whatever happened in its own (sibling exclusion). Every irreducible codeword which contains the
944 * start column and avoids F_0 is found exactly once (one CC hit per codeword), reducible ones at most once. The
945 * choice of the row and the order of the branches depend only on the node, so that the work units (the fixed levels,
946 * see `cc_pack()`: the branch fix[l] among the available columns of the row, with the earlier ones forbidden)
947 * partition the search. The last two levels use the column-syndrome hash, as in cc_walk_last2().
948 * ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ */
949
950/* The column v becomes unavailable (added to S or to F) */
951static inline void bnb_take(cc_walk_t * const t, const int v) {
952 const csr_t * const mHT = t->mHT;
953 const int * const ri = mHT->i, ke = mHT->p[v + 1];
954 int * const acnt = t->acnt;
955 t->X[v >> 6] |= (uint64_t)1 << (v & 63);
956 for (int k = mHT->p[v]; k < ke; k++) acnt[ri[k]]--;
957}
958
959/* The column v becomes available again */
960static inline void bnb_give(cc_walk_t * const t, const int v) {
961 const csr_t * const mHT = t->mHT;
962 const int * const ri = mHT->i, ke = mHT->p[v + 1];
963 int * const acnt = t->acnt;
964 t->X[v >> 6] &= ~((uint64_t)1 << (v & 63));
965 for (int k = mHT->p[v]; k < ke; k++) acnt[ri[k]]++;
966}
967
968static inline bool bnb_avail(const cc_walk_t * const t, const int u) { return u > t->col_min && !bit_get(t->X, u); }
969
970/* bnb_avail() for a column u > col_min (from the position t->kfirst[r] on in its row r) */
971static inline bool bnb_free(const cc_walk_t * const t, const int u) { return !bit_get(t->X, u); }
972
973/* A new generation of the column marks (cleared when the counter wraps around) */
974static inline uint32_t bnb_next_gen(cc_walk_t * const t) {
975 if (++t->gen == 0) {
976 memset(t->mark, 0, (size_t)t->mHT->rows * sizeof(uint32_t));
977 t->gen = 1;
978 }
979 return t->gen;
980}
981
982/* As at the entry of a level: no codeword of weight |S| + extra is recorded once the stop flag is set or the weight
983 * limit has dropped below it (a smaller upper bound) */
984static inline bool bnb_record_ok(const cc_walk_t * const t, const int extra) {
985 distfork_ctx_t * const ctx = t->ctx;
986 if (atomic_load_explicit(&ctx->stop_flag, memory_order_relaxed)) return false;
987 const int cur_dmax = atomic_load_explicit(&ctx->dmax, memory_order_relaxed);
988 return !(cur_dmax > 0 && ctx->p->dW >= 0 && minint(t->w_limit, cur_dmax + ctx->p->dW) < t->w + extra);
989}
990
991/* The packing bound b2 for the nu unsatisfied rows t->ulist (t->uacnt: their amin..amax available columns): a greedy
992 * packing of rows with pairwise disjoint sets of available columns, the rows with the fewest available columns first
993 * (in row order); returns its size once it exceeds R, or once the rows left cannot make it exceed R */
994static int bnb_packing(cc_walk_t * const t, const int R, const int nu, const int amin, const int amax) {
995 int * const bcnt = t->bcnt; /* bcnt[a - amin]: first the number of the rows with a - 1 available columns */
996 const int * const ulist = t->ulist, * const uacnt = t->uacnt;
997 int * const ord = t->ord;
998 const int na = amax - amin + 1;
999 for (int a = 0; a <= na; a++) bcnt[a] = 0;
1000 for (int i = 0; i < nu; i++) bcnt[uacnt[i] - amin + 1]++;
1001 for (int a = 1; a <= na; a++) bcnt[a] += bcnt[a - 1]; /* then the first position of the rows with a */
1002 for (int i = 0; i < nu; i++) ord[bcnt[uacnt[i] - amin]++] = ulist[i];
1003 const uint32_t g = bnb_next_gen(t);
1004 uint32_t * const mark = t->mark; /* the columns of the rows packed so far (the available ones count) */
1005 const uint64_t * const X = t->X;
1006 const int * const rp = t->mH->p, * const ci = t->mH->i, * const kf = t->kfirst;
1007 int cnt = 0;
1008 for (int i = 0; i < nu; i++) {
1009 const int r = ord[i], kb = kf[r], ke = rp[r + 1];
1010 int k = kb;
1011 while (k < ke && !(mark[ci[k]] == g && !bit_get(X, ci[k]))) k++;
1012 if (k == ke) { /* disjoint from the rows packed so far */
1013 if (++cnt > R || cnt + (nu - 1 - i) <= R) return cnt;
1014 for (k = kb; k < ke; k++) mark[ci[k]] = g;
1015 } else if (cnt + (nu - 1 - i) <= R) {
1016 return cnt;
1017 }
1018 }
1019 return cnt;
1020}
1021
1022/* cc_prune=2: the coverage bound b3 (the least t such that the t largest values c_u of the available columns sum to at
1023 * least |s|, where c_u is the number of unsatisfied rows of u) and the fractional cover bound b4 (the sum over the
1024 * unsatisfied rows r of 1 / max c_u over the available columns u of r); true if one of them exceeds R */
1025static bool bnb_cover(cc_walk_t * const t, const int R, const int nu) {
1026 const csr_t * const mH = t->mH;
1027 const uint32_t g = bnb_next_gen(t);
1028 int nt = 0;
1029 for (int i = 0; i < nu; i++) {
1030 const int r = t->ulist[i];
1031 for (int k = t->kfirst[r]; k < mH->p[r + 1]; k++) {
1032 const int u = mH->i[k];
1033 if (!bnb_free(t, u)) continue;
1034 if (t->mark[u] != g) {
1035 t->mark[u] = g;
1036 t->cv[u] = 0;
1037 t->touched[nt++] = u;
1038 }
1039 t->cv[u]++;
1040 }
1041 }
1042 const int D = t->max_col_wt;
1043 int * const hist = t->hist;
1044 for (int c = 0; c <= D; c++) hist[c] = 0;
1045 for (int i = 0; i < nt; i++) hist[t->cv[t->touched[i]]]++;
1046 int need = nu, tc = 0;
1047 for (int c = D; c >= 1 && need > 0; c--) {
1048 if ((long long)hist[c] * c >= need) {
1049 tc += (need + c - 1) / c;
1050 need = 0;
1051 } else {
1052 tc += hist[c];
1053 need -= hist[c] * c;
1054 }
1055 }
1056 if (need > 0 || tc > R) return true;
1057 double sum = 0.0; /* (the rows in row order: the same sum on every thread) */
1058 for (int i = 0; i < nu; i++) {
1059 const int r = t->ulist[i];
1060 int mx = 0;
1061 for (int k = t->kfirst[r]; k < mH->p[r + 1]; k++) {
1062 const int u = mH->i[k];
1063 if (bnb_free(t, u) && t->cv[u] > mx) mx = t->cv[u];
1064 }
1065 if (mx == 0) return true;
1066 sum += 1.0 / mx;
1067 /* the partial sums grow, by at most 1 per row, so that the decision may be known early (the rounding errors are
1068 * far smaller than the margins) */
1069 if (sum > R + 1e-9) return true;
1070 if (sum + (nu - 1 - i) < R + 1e-9 - 1e-7) return false;
1071 }
1072 return false;
1073}
1074
1075/* The hash slot of the key (a syndrome hash, see cc_hash_t), NULL if no nonzero column has this hash */
1076static inline const cc_hash_slot_t *cc_hash_find(const cc_hash_t * const hs, const uint64_t key) {
1077 const uint64_t fb = key & hs->bmask;
1078 if (!((hs->bits[fb >> 6] >> (fb & 63)) & 1)) return NULL;
1079 int j = (int)(key >> hs->tshift);
1080 while (hs->tab[j].cnt > 0 && hs->tab[j].key != key) j = (j + 1) & hs->tmask;
1081 return (hs->tab[j].cnt > 0) ? &hs->tab[j] : NULL;
1082}
1083
1084/* The leaf level of cc_bnb() (one column left, not a fixed level): the available columns u with h_u = s, found by a
1085 * lookup of the hash h of s (verified exactly) */
1086static int bnb_leaf(cc_walk_t * const t, const int sw, const uint64_t h) {
1087 const cc_hash_slot_t * const sl = cc_hash_find(t->hs, h);
1088 if (!sl) return 0;
1089 const csr_t * const mHT = t->mHT;
1090 for (int k = sl->beg; k < sl->beg + sl->cnt; k++) {
1091 const int u = t->hs->cols[k];
1092 if (!bnb_avail(t, u)) continue;
1093 const int pb = mHT->p[u];
1094 if (mHT->p[u + 1] - pb != sw) continue;
1095 int x = 0;
1096 while (x < sw && bit_get(t->S, mHT->i[pb + x])) x++;
1097 if (x < sw) continue;
1098 if (!bnb_record_ok(t, 1)) return 0;
1099 if (cc_walk_found(t, -1, u)) return 1;
1100 }
1101 return 0;
1102}
1103
1104/* The last two levels of cc_bnb() (two columns left, not a fixed level): for each available column v of the branching
1105 * row r (in column order), the available columns u != v with h_u = s + h_v, found by a lookup of the hash h ^ hc[v]
1106 * (verified exactly), give the codewords S + {v, u}, each exactly once (doc/cc_completeness.tex, Proposition "the last
1107 * two extensions by a hash table"; the columns v of the earlier branches need not be forbidden: such a column u has
1108 * a zero in the row r, unlike v) */
1109static int bnb_last2(cc_walk_t * const t, const int sw, const uint64_t h, const int r) {
1110 const cc_hash_t * const hs = t->hs;
1111 const csr_t * const mH = t->mH;
1112 for (int i = t->kfirst[r]; i < mH->p[r + 1]; i++) {
1113 const int v = mH->i[i];
1114 if (!bnb_free(t, v)) continue;
1115 const cc_hash_slot_t * const sl = cc_hash_find(hs, h ^ hs->hc[v]);
1116 if (!sl) continue;
1117 for (int k = sl->beg; k < sl->beg + sl->cnt; k++) {
1118 const int u = hs->cols[k];
1119 if (u == v || !bnb_avail(t, u)) continue;
1120 if (!cc_sum2_equal(t->S, sw, t->mHT, v, u)) continue; /* a hash collision */
1121 if (!bnb_record_ok(t, 2)) return 0;
1122 if (cc_walk_found(t, v, u)) return 1;
1123 }
1124 }
1125 return 0;
1126}
1127
1128/* The branch-and-bound recursion at the node (S, F) with S = t->cols[0..w-1] (syndrome t->S of weight sw > 0, hash
1129 * h), F = the columns of t->X not in S; returns 1 if the run is to stop. On return, t->X, t->acnt, and t->fsp are as
1130 * on entry. */
1131static int cc_bnb(cc_walk_t * const t, const int sw, const uint64_t h) {
1132 distfork_ctx_t * const ctx = t->ctx;
1133 if (atomic_load_explicit(&ctx->stop_flag, memory_order_relaxed)) return 0;
1134 const params_t * const p = ctx->p;
1135 const int w = t->w;
1136 int current_limit = t->w_limit;
1137 const int cur_dmax = atomic_load_explicit(&ctx->dmax, memory_order_relaxed);
1138 if (cur_dmax > 0 && p->dW >= 0) current_limit = minint(t->w_limit, cur_dmax + p->dW);
1139 const int R = current_limit - w; /* the number of columns left */
1140 if (R <= 0 || sw > R * t->max_col_wt) return 0; /* b1 */
1141 if (w >= t->count_w) t->nodes++;
1142 const bool fixed = (w <= t->nfix); /* a fixed level of the work unit */
1143 if (R == 1 && !fixed) return bnb_leaf(t, sw, h);
1144 /* the unsatisfied rows, and the branching row: the one with the fewest available columns, the first in row order */
1145 const int nwords = (t->m + 63) >> 6;
1146 const int * const acnt = t->acnt;
1147 int nu = 0, rbest = -1, abest = INT_MAX, amax = 0;
1148 if (R == 2 && !fixed) { /* (only the branching row is needed) */
1149 for (int k = 0; k < nwords; k++) {
1150 uint64_t x = t->S[k];
1151 while (x) {
1152 const int r = (k << 6) + __builtin_ctzll(x);
1153 x &= x - 1;
1154 const int a = acnt[r];
1155 if (a < abest) {
1156 if (a == 0) return 0; /* a dead end */
1157 abest = a;
1158 rbest = r;
1159 }
1160 }
1161 }
1162 return bnb_last2(t, sw, h, rbest);
1163 }
1164 int * const ulist = t->ulist, * const uacnt = t->uacnt;
1165 for (int k = 0; k < nwords; k++) {
1166 uint64_t x = t->S[k];
1167 while (x) {
1168 const int r = (k << 6) + __builtin_ctzll(x);
1169 x &= x - 1;
1170 const int a = acnt[r];
1171 ulist[nu] = r;
1172 uacnt[nu++] = a;
1173 if (a < abest) {
1174 abest = a;
1175 rbest = r;
1176 }
1177 if (a > amax) amax = a;
1178 }
1179 }
1180 if (abest == 0) return 0; /* a dead end */
1181 if (sw > R && R >= 3) { /* (the packing has at most |s| rows; with R <= 2, the hash levels are cheaper) */
1182 if (bnb_packing(t, R, nu, abest, amax) > R) return 0;
1183 /* (with R = 3, the cover bounds rarely prune what the packing leaves, and cost more than they save) */
1184 if (t->prune >= 2 && R >= 4 && bnb_cover(t, R, nu)) return 0;
1185 }
1186 /* the branches: the available columns of the row rbest, in column order */
1187 const csr_t * const mH = t->mH;
1188 const csr_t * const mHT = t->mHT;
1189 int * const brl = t->brl + (size_t)w * (size_t)t->max_row_wt;
1190 int q = 0;
1191 for (int k = t->kfirst[rbest]; k < mH->p[rbest + 1]; k++) {
1192 const int u = mH->i[k];
1193 if (bnb_free(t, u)) brl[q++] = u;
1194 }
1195 const int fsp0 = t->fsp;
1196 int i_beg = 0, i_end = q;
1197 if (fixed) { /* the branch fix[w-1] only, with the columns of the earlier branches forbidden */
1198 const int d = t->fix[w - 1];
1199 if (d >= q) return 0;
1200 for (int i = 0; i < d; i++) {
1201 bnb_take(t, brl[i]);
1202 t->fstk[t->fsp++] = brl[i];
1203 }
1204 i_beg = d;
1205 i_end = d + 1;
1206 }
1207 const int reach = (R - 1) * t->max_col_wt; /* the largest syndrome weight which R - 1 columns can complete */
1208 const uint64_t * const hc = t->hs->hc;
1209 uint64_t * const S = t->S;
1210 int res = 0;
1211 for (int i = i_beg; i < i_end && !res; i++) {
1212 const int v = brl[i];
1213 const int pb = mHT->p[v], pe = mHT->p[v + 1];
1214 bnb_take(t, v); /* v is in S in its branch, and in F after it, whatever happens in the branch */
1215 t->fstk[t->fsp++] = v;
1216 if (sw - (pe - pb) > reach) continue; /* b1 of the branch: its syndrome weight is at least sw - |h_v| */
1217 int nset = 0; /* the rows of v in s */
1218 for (int k = pb; k < pe; k++) nset += bit_get(S, mHT->i[k]);
1219 const int sw1 = sw + (pe - pb) - 2 * nset;
1220 if (sw1 == 0) { /* a codeword if the cluster has the weight of the limit; nothing is searched below it */
1221 if (R == 1 && bnb_record_ok(t, 1)) res = cc_walk_found(t, -1, v);
1222 continue;
1223 }
1224 if (sw1 > reach) continue;
1225 for (int k = pb; k < pe; k++) bit_flip(S, mHT->i[k]);
1226 t->cols[t->w++] = v;
1227 res = cc_bnb(t, sw1, h ^ hc[v]);
1228 t->w--;
1229 for (int k = pb; k < pe; k++) bit_flip(S, mHT->i[k]);
1230 }
1231 while (t->fsp > fsp0) bnb_give(t, t->fstk[--t->fsp]);
1232 return res;
1233}
1234
1235/* Set up t->acnt and t->kfirst for col_min = c (S and F empty): the columns u > c of each row. The start columns
1236 * claimed by a worker grow within a round, so that both are updated incrementally from a smaller c (the columns
1237 * c' < u <= c are dropped: they are the first columns > c' of their rows); otherwise (a new round, or the expert
1238 * `start` list after other units) they are counted again. */
1239static void bnb_acnt_setup(cc_walk_t * const t, const int c) {
1240 if (t->acnt_col == c) return;
1241 if (t->acnt_col != INT_MIN && t->acnt_col < c) {
1242 const csr_t * const mHT = t->mHT;
1243 for (int u = t->acnt_col + 1; u <= c; u++)
1244 for (int k = mHT->p[u]; k < mHT->p[u + 1]; k++) {
1245 t->acnt[mHT->i[k]]--;
1246 t->kfirst[mHT->i[k]]++;
1247 }
1248 } else {
1249 const csr_t * const mH = t->mH;
1250 for (int r = 0; r < t->m; r++) {
1251 int k = mH->p[r];
1252 while (k < mH->p[r + 1] && mH->i[k] <= c) k++; /* (the columns of a row are sorted) */
1253 t->acnt[r] = mH->p[r + 1] - k;
1254 t->kfirst[r] = k;
1255 }
1256 }
1257 t->acnt_col = c;
1258}
1259
1260/* The CC work unit from the start column `col` with the branch and bound (cc_prune >= 1, w_limit > 1, see cc_bnb()):
1261 * the clusters use only the columns u > col, or with the expert `start` list (unlimited clusters), all columns except
1262 * those listed before `col` (`idx`: its position in the list), which are forbidden: a codeword which contains one of
1263 * them is found from the first one it contains (doc/cc_completeness.tex, Proposition "start lists"). With
1264 * start_scan=1, the listed start columns use only the larger columns, as in the scan of all columns. */
1265static void cc_bnb_unit(cc_walk_t * const t, const int col, const int idx, const int w_limit, const int * const fix,
1266 const int nfix) {
1267 const params_t * const p = t->ctx->p;
1268 const csr_t * const mHT = t->mHT;
1269 const bool list = (p->start_num > 0 && !p->start_scan);
1270 t->col_min = list ? -1 : col;
1271 bnb_acnt_setup(t, t->col_min);
1272 t->fsp = 0;
1273 if (list) {
1274 for (int i = 0; i < idx; i++) {
1275 bnb_take(t, p->start_list[i]);
1276 t->fstk[t->fsp++] = p->start_list[i];
1277 }
1278 bnb_take(t, col); /* (with col_min = col, the start column is not available anyway) */
1279 }
1280 const int pb = mHT->p[col], pe = mHT->p[col + 1];
1281 for (int k = pb; k < pe; k++) bit_flip(t->S, mHT->i[k]);
1282 t->cols[0] = col;
1283 t->w = 1;
1284 t->w_limit = w_limit;
1285 t->fix = fix;
1286 t->nfix = nfix;
1287 t->count_w = nfix + 1; /* (see cc_walk_t: count_w - 1 = the first fixed level with only zero digits from there on) */
1288 while (t->count_w > 1 && fix[t->count_w - 2] == 0) t->count_w--;
1289 cc_bnb(t, pe - pb, t->hs->hc[col]);
1290 t->w = 0;
1291 for (int k = pb; k < pe; k++) bit_flip(t->S, mHT->i[k]);
1292 if (list) bnb_give(t, col);
1293 while (t->fsp > 0) bnb_give(t, t->fstk[--t->fsp]);
1294}
1295
1296/* Recursive CC worker function (interruptible), used with smax > 0 (otherwise, cc_walk() explores the same clusters).
1297 * At the fixed levels w = err->wei <= nfix of a CC work unit (see `cc_pack()`), only the column at position fix[w-1]
1298 * of the row is added (none if the row is shorter). */
1299static int start_CC_recurs_mt(one_vec_t *err, one_vec_t *urr, one_vec_t * const syn[],
1300 const int w_limit, const int max_col_wt,
1301 const csr_t * const mH, const csr_t * const mHT,
1302 worker_arg_t *warg, const int * const fix, const int nfix) {
1303 distfork_ctx_t *ctx = warg->ctx;
1304 if (atomic_load_explicit(&ctx->stop_flag, memory_order_relaxed)) {
1305 return 0;
1306 }
1307 params_t * const p = ctx->p;
1308 const int w = err->wei;
1309 int current_limit = w_limit;
1310 int cur_dmax = atomic_load_explicit(&ctx->dmax, memory_order_relaxed);
1311 if (cur_dmax > 0 && p->dW >= 0) {
1312 current_limit = minint(w_limit, cur_dmax + p->dW);
1313 }
1314 if (w >= current_limit) {
1315 return 0;
1316 }
1317
1318 const one_vec_t * const syn_w = syn[w];
1319 const int syn_w_wei = syn_w->wei;
1320 const int row = syn_w->vec[0];
1321 /* the positions in mH of the columns of the row to add: all of them, or one at a fixed level of the work unit */
1322 int i1_beg = mH->p[row], i1_end = mH->p[row + 1];
1323 if (w <= nfix) {
1324 i1_beg += fix[w - 1];
1325 if (i1_beg >= i1_end) return 0;
1326 i1_end = i1_beg + 1;
1327 }
1328 const colmask_t * const mL = p->maskL; /* NULL for a classical code */
1329 /* Clusters are grown only to columns larger than the start column, except with the expert `start`
1330 * list, where clusters are unlimited (columns already in `err` are skipped via `one_ordered_search`),
1331 * unless start_scan=1. */
1332 const int col_min = (p->start_num > 0 && !p->start_scan) ? -1 : urr->vec[0];
1333
1334 /* Leaf level: w + 1 == current_limit */
1335 if (w + 1 == current_limit) {
1336 int max_leaf_swei = 0;
1337 if (p->smax > 0 && current_limit < MAX_W) {
1338 int cur_min = warg->min_swei[current_limit] - 1;
1339 max_leaf_swei = (cur_min < p->smax) ? (cur_min > 0 ? cur_min : 0) : p->smax;
1340 }
1341
1342 for (int i1 = i1_beg; i1 < i1_end; i1++) {
1343 const int col = mH->i[i1];
1344 if (col <= col_min) continue;
1345
1346 const int p_beg = mHT->p[col];
1347 const int col_wt = mHT->p[col + 1] - p_beg;
1348 if (abs(syn_w_wei - col_wt) > max_leaf_swei) continue;
1349
1350 int swei;
1351 if (max_leaf_swei == 0) {
1352 /* Only swei == 0 is of interest: check if mHT[col] == syn[w] */
1353 if (mHT->i[p_beg] != row ||
1354 mHT->i[p_beg + col_wt - 1] != syn_w->vec[col_wt - 1]) {
1355 continue;
1356 }
1357 if (memcmp(syn_w->vec, &mHT->i[p_beg], (size_t)col_wt * sizeof(int)) != 0) {
1358 continue;
1359 }
1360 if (one_ordered_search(err, col) != -1) continue;
1361 swei = 0;
1362 } else {
1363 if (one_ordered_search(err, col) != -1) continue;
1364 syn[w + 1]->wei = 0;
1365 swei = one_csr_row_combine(syn[w + 1], syn_w, mHT, col);
1366 if (swei > 0) {
1367 if (swei <= max_leaf_swei) {
1368 warg->min_swei[w + 1] = swei;
1369 int cur_min = swei - 1;
1370 max_leaf_swei = (cur_min < p->smax) ? (cur_min > 0 ? cur_min : 0) : p->smax;
1371 }
1372 continue;
1373 }
1374 }
1375
1376 /* swei == 0: insert col into err to verify against mL and record codeword */
1377 int pos = one_ordered_ins(err, col);
1378 int nz = (!mL) || colmask_syndrome_non_zero(mL, err->wei, err->vec);
1379 if (nz && cc_record(ctx, warg, err)) {
1380 one_ordered_pos_del(err, col, pos);
1381 return 1;
1382 }
1383 one_ordered_pos_del(err, col, pos);
1384 }
1385 return 0;
1386 }
1387
1388 /* Internal level: w + 1 < current_limit */
1389 const int rem = current_limit - (w + 1);
1390 int max_s_needed = 0;
1391 if (p->smax > 0 && current_limit < MAX_W) { /* smax > 0 only without noscan and with dmin <= 1 (var_init) */
1392 int cur_min = warg->min_swei[current_limit] - 1;
1393 max_s_needed = (cur_min < p->smax) ? (cur_min > 0 ? cur_min : 0) : p->smax;
1394 }
1395 const int max_reach = rem * max_col_wt + max_s_needed;
1396
1397 for (int i1 = i1_beg; i1 < i1_end; i1++) {
1398 const int col = mH->i[i1];
1399 if (col > col_min) {
1400 const int col_wt = mHT->p[col + 1] - mHT->p[col];
1401 if (syn_w_wei - col_wt > max_reach) continue;
1402
1403 int pos = one_ordered_search(err, col);
1404 if (pos == -1) {
1405 syn[w + 1]->wei = 0;
1406 int swei = one_csr_row_combine(syn[w + 1], syn_w, mHT, col);
1407
1408 if (p->smax && swei > 0 && swei <= p->smax && (w + 1 < MAX_W)) {
1409 if (swei < warg->min_swei[w + 1]) {
1410 warg->min_swei[w + 1] = swei;
1411 }
1412 }
1413
1414 if (swei > 0 && swei <= max_reach) {
1415 urr->vec[w] = col;
1416 urr->wei++;
1417 pos = one_ordered_ins(err, col);
1418 int result = start_CC_recurs_mt(err, urr, syn, w_limit, max_col_wt,
1419 mH, mHT, warg, fix, nfix);
1420 urr->wei--;
1421 one_ordered_pos_del(err, col, pos);
1422 if (result == 1) {
1423 return 1;
1424 }
1425 }
1426 }
1427 }
1428 }
1429 return 0;
1430}
1431
1432/* The window of a hybrid RW step (kwin=0, n >= 500: an index window on every other global step), see
1433 * rw_hybrid_window() in util_io.h */
1434static inline int hybrid_window(const params_t * const p, const int nvar) {
1435 return rw_hybrid_window(p, nvar);

1438/* Add the thread time `*acc_t` of `*acc_n` completed RW steps to the totals of the RW timing model, and reset them */
1439static inline void rw_time_publish(distfork_ctx_t *ctx, double *acc_t, int *acc_n) {
1440 if (*acc_n > 0) {
1441 atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&ctx->rw_busy_ns, (long long)(*acc_t * 1e9), memory_order_relaxed);
1442 atomic_fetch_add_explicit(&ctx->rw_timed_steps, *acc_n, memory_order_relaxed);
1443 }
1444 *acc_t = 0.0;
1445 *acc_n = 0;
1446}
1447
1448/* Time of a completed RW step since `*t_last`: published at least every 2 ms (after every step if steps are slow),
1449 * and right away for the first step of a batch (`first`), so that the coordinator gets the step time early */
1450static inline void rw_time_step(distfork_ctx_t *ctx, double *t_last, double *acc_t, int *acc_n, const bool first) {
1451 const double t_now = get_time_sec();
1452 *acc_t += t_now - *t_last;
1453 *t_last = t_now;
1454 (*acc_n)++;
1455 if (first || *acc_t >= 0.002) rw_time_publish(ctx, acc_t, acc_n);
1456}

1458/* Weight limit (exclusive) of the RW candidate codewords, see codeword_rw_limit() */
1459static inline int rw_cw_limit(distfork_ctx_t * const ctx) {
1460 return codeword_rw_limit(ctx->p, atomic_load_explicit(&ctx->dmax, memory_order_relaxed),
1461 atomic_load_explicit(&ctx->cw_feed_limit, memory_order_relaxed));
1462}
1463
1464/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1465 * steplog=FILE (study option): the log of the full-matrix RW steps (ksub=0) and of the codewords recorded in them, for
1466 * the statistics of the step types (the format is in the help of steplog). Each RW thread collects the codewords
1467 * recorded in its current step (steplog_cw() in rw_record_locked(), under `cw_mutex`) and writes all lines of the step
1468 * at its end (steplog_step_end()) under the mutex of the log, which also guards the set of the keys logged: the first
1469 * line of a key has the support. The keys are those of rec_add() (rw_set_key() with the Zobrist values of
1470 * rw_zobrist_cols(), fixed: the same in every run on the same matrix), the canonical keys those of rw_canon_key()
1471 * (Stage 5), computed once per codeword and thread, outside the mutexes. Off by default: then only the tests of
1472 * ctx->steplog and warg->slt (NULL) remain in the RW steps.
1473 * ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ */
1474#define STEPLOG_SEEN_MAX (1u << 23) /* at most this many keys get their supports logged (then none) */
1475#define STEPLOG_CACHE_MAX (1u << 20) /* at most this many canonical keys are cached per thread */
1476
1477typedef struct steplog {
1478 FILE *f;
1479 pthread_mutex_t mtx; /* guards the file, the set of the keys logged, and the counts */
1480 const uint64_t *zcol; /* the Zobrist values of the columns (ctx->zcol, or own_zcol) */
1481 uint64_t *own_zcol; /* (without the RW stages of rw_opt) */
1482 uint64_t *seen; /* the keys logged with their supports (open addressing, 0: an empty slot) */
1483 uint32_t smask, nseen;
1484 int seen_full; /* STEPLOG_SEEN_MAX keys logged: no more supports */
1485 long long nsteps, ncw; /* the lines S and C written */
1486} steplog_t;
1487
1488typedef struct steplog_thr {
1489 int n, cap; /* the codewords recorded in the current step: their weights, flags (see steplog_cw()), */
1490 int *w; /* origins, keys, canonical keys, and supports pool[off..off+w-1] */
1491 char *flag, *org;
1492 uint64_t *key, *ckey;
1493 size_t *off;
1494 int *pool;
1495 size_t plen, pcap;
1496 char *out; /* the lines of the step */
1497 size_t olen, ocap;
1498 uint64_t *ck, *cv; /* the canonical keys computed by this thread (open addressing by the key, 0: empty) */
1499 uint32_t cmask, ncache;
1500 double t0; /* the start of the current step */
1501 int open; /* 1: a step is started and not logged yet */
1502 int orig; /* the origin of the codeword recorded next: 1 a single column (p=1), 2 a pair (p=2), plus 4
1503 * for its shortened form (Stage 2, see rw_candidate()) */
1504} steplog_thr_t;
1505
1506static void *steplog_realloc(void * const ptr, const size_t size) {
1507 void * const q = realloc(ptr, size);
1508 if (!q) ERROR("memory allocation");
1509 return q;
1510}
1511
1512static inline uint32_t steplog_slot(const uint64_t key, const uint32_t mask) {
1513 return (uint32_t)(key ^ (key >> 32)) & mask;
1514}
1515
1516static steplog_thr_t *steplog_thr_free(steplog_thr_t * const s) {
1517 if (!s) return NULL;
1518 free(s->w);
1519 free(s->flag);
1520 free(s->org);
1521 free(s->key);
1522 free(s->ckey);
1523 free(s->off);
1524 free(s->pool);
1525 free(s->out);
1526 free(s->ck);
1527 free(s->cv);
1528 free(s);
1529 return NULL;
1530}
1531
1532/* A new step of the thread */
1533static inline void steplog_step_begin(steplog_thr_t * const s) {
1534 s->n = 0;
1535 s->plen = 0;
1536 s->open = 1;
1537 s->t0 = get_time_sec();
1538}
1539
1540/* The codeword ee (sorted, cnt columns) recorded in the current step of the thread (under `cw_mutex`): `flag` n (new in
1541 * the codeword hash), o (a codeword in hash: one more hit), or x (not kept, see codeword_add_maybe()); its origin is
1542 * s->orig, set by the caller */
1543static void steplog_cw(const steplog_t * const sl, steplog_thr_t * const s, const int * const ee, const int cnt,
1544 const char flag) {
1545 if (s->n == s->cap) {
1546 s->cap = s->cap ? 2 * s->cap : 64;
1547 s->w = steplog_realloc(s->w, (size_t)s->cap * sizeof(int));
1548 s->flag = steplog_realloc(s->flag, (size_t)s->cap);
1549 s->org = steplog_realloc(s->org, (size_t)s->cap);
1550 s->key = steplog_realloc(s->key, (size_t)s->cap * sizeof(uint64_t));
1551 s->ckey = steplog_realloc(s->ckey, (size_t)s->cap * sizeof(uint64_t));
1552 s->off = steplog_realloc(s->off, (size_t)s->cap * sizeof(size_t));
1553 }
1554 if (s->plen + (size_t)cnt > s->pcap) {
1555 s->pcap = 2 * (s->plen + (size_t)cnt) + 1024;
1556 s->pool = steplog_realloc(s->pool, s->pcap * sizeof(int));
1557 }
1558 const int i = s->n++;
1559 s->w[i] = cnt;
1560 s->flag[i] = flag;
1561 s->org[i] = (char)('0' + s->orig);
1562 s->key[i] = rw_set_key(sl->zcol, ee, cnt, 0x2545f4914f6cdd1dULL); /* (as in rec_add()) */
1563 s->ckey[i] = 0;
1564 s->off[i] = s->plen;
1565 memcpy(s->pool + s->plen, ee, (size_t)cnt * sizeof(int));
1566 s->plen += (size_t)cnt;
1567}
1568
1569/* Record the RW codeword `ee` of weight `cnt` (sorted indices) found in a step with a uniform random permutation, with
1570 * a window, or in a row slab (`src`: CW_SRC_RW_UNIFORM, CW_SRC_RW_WINDOW, or CW_SRC_RW_SLAB): add it to the hash (or
1571 * count one more hit), update the upper bound dmax and the stop flags (`ksub` > 0 only for the message).
1572 * rw_record_locked() is the part under `cw_mutex` before the stop checks of rw_record_checks(), which can follow
1573 * several codewords (see rw_rec_flush()). */
1574static void rw_record_locked(distfork_ctx_t * const ctx, const rci_t * const ee, const int cnt, const int tid,
1575 const int ksub, const int src) {
1576 params_t * const p = ctx->p;
1577 /* with outC or maxC, codewords are collected: RW does not end the run when the bounds coincide or on wmin (in
1578 * method 3, the coordinator then runs the CC rounds which enumerate the codewords) */
1579 const bool collecting = (p->outC != NULL) || (p->maxC > 0);
1580 steplog_thr_t * const slt = ctx->steplog ? ctx->wargs[tid].slt : NULL; /* (steplog=FILE: NULL with ksub > 0) */
1581 const int cnt0 = slt ? codeword_count(p, ee, cnt) : 0;
1582 p->codewords = codeword_add_maybe(p, ee, cnt, src);
1583 if (res.on && cnt == p->min_w) res_witness_set(ee, cnt, "rw");
1584 if (slt) steplog_cw(ctx->steplog, slt, ee, cnt, cnt0 ? 'o' : (codeword_count(p, ee, cnt) ? 'n' : 'x'));
1585 ctx_update_feed_limit(ctx);
1586 const int best = p->min_w; /* a codeword lighter than min_w is always added */
1587 const int old_dmax = atomic_load(&ctx->dmax);
1588 if (old_dmax == 0 || best < old_dmax) {
1589 atomic_store(&ctx->dmax, best);
1590 const double t_now = (p->stamp || res.on) ? (get_time_sec() - ctx->start_time) : 0.0;
1591 if (res.on) res_event_ctx_at(ctx, t_now);
1592 if (p->debug & DBG_PROGRESS) {
1593 const tstamp_t ts = tstamp_at(p, t_now);
1594 int num_rw = (p->method == 1) ? ctx->num_threads
1595 : minint(ctx->rw_threads, ctx->num_threads - atomic_load(&ctx->cc_target_workers));
1596 if (num_rw < 1) num_rw = 1;
1597 if (ksub > 0) {
1598 fprintf(stderr, "# [thread %d] RW (ksub=%d) found new upper bound cw of weight %d (using %d RW threads)%s\n",
1599 tid, ksub, best, num_rw, ts.s);
1600 } else {
1601 fprintf(stderr, "# [thread %d] RW found new upper bound cw of weight %d (using %d RW threads)%s\n",
1602 tid, best, num_rw, ts.s);
1603 }
1604 }
1605 if ((p->debug & DBG_CODEWORDS) && cnt == best) {
1606 char prefix[48];
1607 snprintf(prefix, sizeof(prefix), "# [thread %d] RW codeword", tid);
1608 print_codeword_support(stderr, prefix, ee, cnt, p->debug);
1609 }
1610 const int cur_dmin = atomic_load(&ctx->dmin);
1611 if (!collecting && cur_dmin > 0 && best <= cur_dmin) {
1612 ctx_stop(ctx, STOP_BOUNDS);
1613 }
1614 }
1615}
1616
1617static void rw_record_checks(distfork_ctx_t * const ctx) {
1618 params_t * const p = ctx->p;
1619 const bool collecting = (p->outC != NULL) || (p->maxC > 0);
1620 const int best = p->min_w;
1621 if (!collecting && p->wmin > 0 && best <= p->wmin) {
1622 ctx_stop(ctx, STOP_WMIN);
1623 }
1624 if (codeword_maxc_reached(p)) {
1625 ctx_stop(ctx, STOP_MAXC);
1626 }
1627 if (check_min_hits_convergence(p)) {
1628 if ((p->debug & DBG_PROGRESS) && !atomic_load(&ctx->stop_flag) && !atomic_load(&ctx->rw_stop_flag)) {
1629 const tstamp_t ts = tstamp_now(ctx);
1630 if (p->canon.active && !p->canon.full) {
1631 const rw_canon_stats_t * const cs = &p->canon;
1632 fprintf(stderr,
1633 "# RW convergence reached: canonical classes of weight %d in the uniform steps: %lld classes, %lld "
1634 "step incidences (%.2f >= min_hits=%d per class), f1=%lld, f2=%lld, p_GT=%.3g%s\n",
1635 cs->w, cs->classes, cs->n_unif, (double)cs->n_unif / (double)cs->classes, p->min_hits, cs->f1,
1636 cs->f2, (double)cs->f1 / (double)cs->n_unif, ts.s);
1637 } else {
1638 cw_hit_stats_t st;
1639 codeword_hit_stats(p, &st);
1640 char excl[64] = "";
1641 if (st.excl_hits > 0) /* (see rw_nhits_sources()) */
1642 snprintf(excl, sizeof(excl), "; %lld window and slab hits not counted", st.excl_hits);
1643 fprintf(stderr,
1644 "# RW convergence reached: <n>=%.2f >= min_hits=%d average hits per codeword (%lld cws of weight "
1645 "%d..%d; w=%d: %lld cws, %lld hits), P_fail ~ exp(-<n>) = %.2g%s%s\n", st.avg, p->min_hits,
1646 st.set_cws, st.w_lo, st.w_hi, st.w_lo, st.min_cws, st.min_hits, exp(-st.avg), excl, ts.s);
1647 }
1648 }
1649 if (p->method == 1) {
1650 ctx_stop(ctx, STOP_RW_CONVERGED);
1651 } else {
1652 atomic_store(&ctx->rw_stop_flag, true);
1653 }
1654 }
1655}
1656
1657static void rw_record_codeword(distfork_ctx_t * const ctx, const rci_t * const ee, const int cnt, const int tid,
1658 const int ksub, const int src) {
1659 pthread_mutex_lock(&ctx->cw_mutex);
1660 rw_record_locked(ctx, ee, cnt, tid, ksub, src);
1661 rw_record_checks(ctx);
1662 pthread_mutex_unlock(&ctx->cw_mutex);
1663}
1664
1665/* dst ^= src, and dst = a ^ b, for rows of `width` words */
1666static inline void rw_row_xor(word * __restrict dst, const word * __restrict src, const wi_t width) {
1667 for (wi_t w = 0; w < width; w++) dst[w] ^= src[w];
1668}
1669static inline void rw_row_xor3(word * __restrict dst, const word * __restrict a, const word * __restrict b,
1670 const wi_t width) {
1671 for (wi_t w = 0; w < width; w++) dst[w] = a[w] ^ b[w];
1672}
1673
1674#define RW_K_MAX 8 /* at most 2^8 rows per table of rw_eliminate() */
1675#define RW_NT_MAX 8 /* at most 8 tables, i.e., 64 pivots per pass over the rows */
1676
1677/* Parameters of rw_eliminate() for a matrix of `rows` x `width` words: the number of tables `*nt` and of pivots per
1678 * table `*k` (column by column: *nt = 0, below 128 rows). For wide rows, the tables are kept at about 2 MB or less
1679 * (cache): fewer rows per table, more tables. Measured (single thread): K = 6 with 4 tables is 1.7x to 2.2x faster
1680 * than column by column for 648 to 2736 rows (circuit DEMs, a 1500 x 3000 LDPC code), also with 16 threads; between
1681 * 128 and 512 rows, K = 5 with 4 tables is 0.75x to 1.4x as fast, depending on the matrix (see rw_elim_t). */
1682static void rw_block_params(const int rows, const wi_t width, int * const k, int * const nt) {
1683 *k = 0;
1684 *nt = 0;
1685 if (rows < 128) return;
1686 *k = (rows < 512) ? 5 : 6;
1687 *nt = 4;
1688 while (*k > 3 && ((size_t)*nt << *k) * (size_t)width * sizeof(word) > ((size_t)2 << 20)) {
1689 (*k)--;
1690 if (*nt + 2 <= RW_NT_MAX) *nt += 2;
1691 }
1692}
1693
1694/* RW elimination of a thread: the tables and parameters of rw_eliminate(), and the choice between it and the column-by-
1695 * column elimination for 128 to 512 rows, where the blocked one is not always faster: the steps 1..2*RW_TUNE_STEPS
1696 * (after the first one, from the sparse H) alternate between the two eliminations, which give the same results, and
1697 * the faster one (in total) is used for the following steps */
1698#define RW_TUNE_STEPS 4
1699typedef struct {
1700 word *table; /* the tables of rw_eliminate(): nt << k rows of tstride words, row 0 of each table zero */
1701 size_t tstride;
1702 int k, nt; /* pivots per table, number of tables (0: column by column), see rw_block_params() */
1703 int steps; /* RW steps completed while tuning */
1704 double t[2]; /* time of the timed eliminations: column by column (0), blocked (1) */
1705 int choice; /* -1: tuning, 0: column by column, 1: blocked */
1706} rw_elim_t;
1707
1708/* RW elimination with the "Method of the Four Russians" (as in M4RI's echelonization, but for the scattered columns
1709 * of a random permutation): Gauss-Jordan elimination of the columns order[0], order[1], ... in the rows
1710 * 0..nrows_eff-1 of M, until nrows_eff pivots are found, in blocks of up to nt*K pivots.
1711 * 1. The pivots of a block, in the order of the columns: a column is a pivot if a row r >= rank, reduced with the
1712 * previous pivots, has a 1 in it. The block's pivot rows are kept reduced with each other, so that the reduced bit
1713 * of a row is its bit plus the parity of its bits in the pivot columns of the block's pivot rows with a 1 in the
1714 * column: the rows are searched without row operations, and only the new pivot row is reduced.
1715 * 2. Tables of the 2^K combinations of K pivot rows each (built with one row XOR each, in Gray-code order; row 0 of
1716 * each table is zero; table t at T + (t << K) * tstride, see rw_elim_t).
1717 * 3. Every other row is reduced in one pass: for each table, the combination given by the row's bits in its pivot
1718 * columns (the row stays in the L1 cache, while it is read and written only once from memory).
1719 * The pivots, their rows, and the reduced matrix are the same as with gauss_one_rows() column by column, with about
1720 * 1/(nt*K) of the passes over the rows of M. The pivot columns are stored in pivs[0..rank-1] and set in piv_mask.
1721 * Returns the rank, or -1 if interrupted by a stop flag (checked every 16 columns, as before). (Not inlined, so that
1722 * the column-by-column elimination in run_rw_steps() stays as compact as before for small matrices.) */
1723__attribute__((noinline))
1724static int rw_eliminate(distfork_ctx_t * const ctx, mzd_t * const M, const int nrows_eff, const int nvar,
1725 const rci_t * const order, rci_t * const pivs, word * const piv_mask,
1726 const rw_elim_t * const el) {
1727 word * const T = el->table;
1728 const size_t tstride = el->tstride;
1729 const int K = el->k, nt = el->nt;
1730 const wi_t width = M->width;
1731 const int P = K * nt; /* pivots per block */
1732 int bw[RW_K_MAX * RW_NT_MAX], bs[RW_K_MAX * RW_NT_MAX]; /* word and bit of the pivot columns of the block */
1733 int rank = 0;
1734 int i = 0;
1735 while (i < nvar && rank < nrows_eff) {
1736 const int r0 = rank; /* the first pivot row of the block */
1737 int kk = 0;
1738 /* 1. up to P pivots */
1739 while (kk < P && i < nvar && rank < nrows_eff) {
1740 if ((i & 15) == 15 && (atomic_load_explicit(&ctx->stop_flag, memory_order_relaxed) ||
1741 atomic_load_explicit(&ctx->rw_stop_flag, memory_order_relaxed))) {
1742 return -1;
1743 }
1744 const int col = order[i++];
1745 const int cw = col >> 6, cb = col & 63;
1746 uint64_t mask = 0; /* the block's pivot rows with a 1 in the column */
1747 for (int l = 0; l < kk; l++) mask |= (uint64_t)((mzd_row(M, r0 + l)[cw] >> cb) & 1) << l;
1748 int found = -1;
1749 for (int r = rank; r < nrows_eff; r++) {
1750 const word * const row = mzd_row(M, r);
1751 word b = (row[cw] >> cb) & 1;
1752 for (uint64_t m2 = mask; m2; m2 &= m2 - 1) {
1753 const int l = __builtin_ctzll(m2);
1754 b ^= (row[bw[l]] >> bs[l]) & 1;
1755 }
1756 if (b) {
1757 found = r;
1758 break;
1759 }
1760 }
1761 if (found < 0) continue; /* not a pivot: the column depends on the previous ones */
1762 if (found != rank) mzd_row_swap(M, rank, found);
1763 word * const prow = mzd_row(M, rank);
1764 for (int l = 0; l < kk; l++) { /* reduce the new pivot row with the block's pivot rows */
1765 if ((prow[bw[l]] >> bs[l]) & 1) rw_row_xor(prow, mzd_row(M, r0 + l), width);
1766 }
1767 for (uint64_t m2 = mask; m2; m2 &= m2 - 1) /* and clear the column in them */
1768 rw_row_xor(mzd_row(M, r0 + __builtin_ctzll(m2)), prow, width);
1769 bw[kk] = cw;
1770 bs[kk] = cb;
1771 kk++;
1772 pivs[rank] = col;
1773 piv_mask[cw] |= (word)1 << cb;
1774 rank++;
1775 }
1776 if (kk == 0) break; /* no more columns */
1777 /* 2. the tables: row g of table t is the sum of the pivot rows r0 + t*K + l of the bits l of g */
1778 const int ntab = (kk + K - 1) / K;
1779 for (int t = 0; t < ntab; t++) {
1780 word * const Tt = T + ((size_t)t << K) * tstride;
1781 const int kt = (kk - t * K < K) ? kk - t * K : K;
1782 for (unsigned g = 1; g < (1u << kt); g++) {
1783 const unsigned gc = g ^ (g >> 1), gp = (g - 1) ^ ((g - 1) >> 1); /* Gray codes of g and g-1 */
1784 rw_row_xor3(Tt + gc * tstride, Tt + gp * tstride, mzd_row(M, r0 + t * K + __builtin_ctz(g)), width);
1785 }
1786 }
1787 /* 3. all other rows, in one pass */
1788 for (int r = 0; r < nrows_eff; r++) {
1789 if (r == r0) {
1790 r = rank - 1; /* (the pivot rows of the block) */
1791 continue;
1792 }
1793 word * const row = mzd_row(M, r);
1794 unsigned x[RW_NT_MAX];
1795 for (int t = 0; t < ntab; t++) { /* (the bits first: the XORs change the row's bits in the pivot columns) */
1796 const int lo = t * K, hi = (lo + K < kk) ? lo + K : kk;
1797 unsigned xt = 0;
1798 for (int l = lo; l < hi; l++) xt |= (unsigned)((row[bw[l]] >> bs[l]) & 1) << (l - lo);
1799 x[t] = xt;
1800 }
1801 for (int t = 0; t < ntab; t++) {
1802 if (x[t]) rw_row_xor(row, T + (((size_t)t << K) + x[t]) * tstride, width);
1803 }
1804 }
1805 }
1806 return rank;
1807}
1808
1809/* The RW pairs (p=2), see rw_pairs_bits(): a RW step also finds the codewords with exactly two non-pivot columns a, b,
1810 * the sums of the codewords of a and b (p=1), whose pivot part is the sum of the columns a and b of the reduced matrix.
1811 * The non-pivot columns are sorted by their bits in l random pivot rows (the bucket, as in Stern's algorithm), and only
1812 * the pairs in a bucket are checked. In a bucket, the columns are sorted by weight, so that only the pairs whose
1813 * weights differ by less than the weight limit are checked (the weight of the sum is at least the difference), and the
1814 * columns whose codewords have a zero L syndrome come first: the pairs of two of them are skipped (the codewords of
1815 * most columns of a circuit DEM are light and local, with a zero L syndrome), and so are the pairs with equal L
1816 * syndromes. With at most 64 rows of L, the L syndromes of all columns are known (the rows of L reduced with the pivot
1817 * rows); otherwise, only those of the light columns (a hash, see rw_lhash_init()). */
1818typedef struct {
1819 const word *row; /* the column in the pivot rows (a row of the transposed reduced matrix) */
1820 uint64_t sig; /* the L syndrome of the column's codeword (or its hash, see rw_lhash_init()), if known */
1821 int col; /* the column */
1822 int known; /* 1 if `sig` is known */
1823} rw_pair_t;
1824
1825/* LSD radix sort (8-bit digits) of `n` keys `a` by their lowest `bits` bits (`tmp`: n more) */
1826static void rw_radix_sort(uint64_t * const a, uint64_t * const tmp, const int n, const int bits) {
1827 uint64_t *src = a, *dst = tmp;
1828 for (int sh = 0; sh < bits; sh += 8) {
1829 int cnt[256];
1830 memset(cnt, 0, sizeof(cnt));
1831 for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) cnt[(src[i] >> sh) & 255]++;
1832 for (int d = 0, sum = 0; d < 256; d++) {
1833 const int c = cnt[d];
1834 cnt[d] = sum;
1835 sum += c;
1836 }
1837 for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) dst[cnt[(src[i] >> sh) & 255]++] = src[i];
1838 uint64_t * const t = src;
1839 src = dst;
1840 dst = t;
1841 }
1842 if (src != a) memcpy(a, src, (size_t)n * sizeof(uint64_t));
1843}
1844
1845/* The workspace of a thread for the RW pairs (see rw_pair_t, rw_pairs_step()) */
1846typedef struct {
1847 rw_pair_t *ent; /* the entries of the non-pivot columns (nvar of them) */
1848 uint64_t *srt; /* their sort keys (bucket, zero L syndrome or not, weight, entry), 2 nvar for the radix sort */
1849 int nl; /* the number of rows of L if at most 64 (0: a classical code, or more rows) */
1850 wi_t width; /* the words per row of the RW matrix (with nl > 0) */
1851 word *lrows; /* with nl > 0: the rows of L (nl rows of `width` words) */
1852 word *srows; /* and the rows of L reduced with the pivot rows of a RW step: the L syndromes of the codewords */
1853} rw_pairs_ws_t;
1854
1855/* The hashes of the columns of L for the RW pairs (see rw_pair_t): the hash of the L syndrome of a vector is the sum of
1856 * the hashes of its columns. With at most 64 rows of L, the hash of a column is its mask (the syndrome itself);
1857 * otherwise, the sum of 64-bit random hashes of its rows (a non-zero syndrome has the hash zero with probability
1858 * 2^-64). NULL for a classical code. */
1859static uint64_t *rw_lhash_init(const params_t * const p) {
1860 const colmask_t * const cm = p->maskL;
1861 const int nvar = p->spaH->cols;
1862 if (p->classical || !cm || cm->cols < nvar) return NULL;
1863 uint64_t * const h = malloc((size_t)nvar * sizeof(uint64_t));
1864 if (!h) ERROR("memory allocation");
1865 if (cm->kw == 1) {
1866 for (int j = 0; j < nvar; j++) h[j] = cm->mask[j];
1867 } else {
1868 uint64_t * const R = malloc((size_t)cm->kw * 64 * sizeof(uint64_t));
1869 if (!R) ERROR("memory allocation");
1870 uint64_t st = mix64((uint64_t)p->seed ^ 0x2545f4914f6cdd1dULL);
1871 for (int t = 0; t < cm->kw * 64; t++) R[t] = splitmix64(&st);
1872 for (int j = 0; j < nvar; j++) {
1873 uint64_t s = 0;
1874 for (int w = 0; w < cm->kw; w++) {
1875 for (word m = cm->mask[(size_t)j * cm->kw + w]; m; m &= m - 1) s ^= R[w * 64 + __builtin_ctzll(m)];
1876 }
1877 h[j] = s;
1878 }
1879 free(R);
1880 }
1881 return h;
1882}
1883
1884/* The workspace of the RW pairs of a thread (`ws->ent` NULL without pairs), for the RW matrix `mH` (`nvar` columns) */
1885static void rw_pairs_ws_init(rw_pairs_ws_t * const ws, const distfork_ctx_t * const ctx, const mzd_t * const mH,
1886 const int nvar) {
1887 memset(ws, 0, sizeof(*ws));
1888 if (ctx->p->pairs == 0 && !ctx->rw_active) return; /* (rw_opt: the L syndromes of single columns, rw_srows()) */
1889 if (ctx->p->pairs != 0) {
1890 ws->ent = malloc((size_t)nvar * sizeof(rw_pair_t));
1891 ws->srt = malloc((size_t)2 * nvar * sizeof(uint64_t));
1892 if (!ws->ent || !ws->srt) ERROR("memory allocation");
1893 }
1894 const colmask_t * const cm = ctx->p->maskL;
1895 if (mH && ctx->rw_lhash && cm->kw == 1 && cm->rows > 0) { /* (not with the sparse-dual elimination, mH NULL) */
1896 ws->nl = cm->rows;
1897 ws->width = mH->width;
1898 ws->lrows = calloc((size_t)ws->nl * ws->width, sizeof(word));
1899 ws->srows = malloc((size_t)ws->nl * ws->width * sizeof(word));
1900 if (!ws->lrows || !ws->srows) ERROR("memory allocation");
1901 for (int j = 0; j < nvar; j++) {
1902 for (word m = cm->mask[j]; m; m &= m - 1)
1903 ws->lrows[(size_t)__builtin_ctzll(m) * ws->width + (j >> 6)] |= (word)1 << (j & 63);
1904 }
1905 }
1906}
1907
1908static void rw_pairs_ws_free(rw_pairs_ws_t * const ws) {
1909 free(ws->ent);
1910 free(ws->srt);
1911 free(ws->lrows);
1912 free(ws->srows);
1913 memset(ws, 0, sizeof(*ws));
1914}
1915
1916/* A codeword of weight `cnt` found by RW is a hit (see rw_hits1, rw_hits2) if not heavier than the upper bound */
1917static inline bool rw_is_hit(distfork_ctx_t * const ctx, const int cnt) {
1918 const int dmax = atomic_load_explicit(&ctx->dmax, memory_order_relaxed);
1919 return (dmax <= 0) || (cnt <= dmax);
1920}
1921
1922/* Weight limit (exclusive) of the codewords of the RW pairs: as for the single columns (rw_cw_limit()), but at most the
1923 * upper bound plus one (plus dW with outC or maxC), and 0 without an upper bound: the pairs would otherwise give far
1924 * too many candidates (of any weight, or the heavier codewords of the `min_hits` statistic) */
1925static inline int rw_pairs_limit(distfork_ctx_t * const ctx) {
1926 const params_t * const p = ctx->p;
1927 const int dmax = atomic_load_explicit(&ctx->dmax, memory_order_relaxed);
1928 if (dmax <= 0) return 0;
1929 long long int cap = (long long int)dmax + 1;
1930 if ((p->outC != NULL || p->maxC > 0) && p->dW > 0) cap += p->dW;
1931 const int lim = rw_cw_limit(ctx);
1932 return (lim < cap) ? lim : (int)cap;
1933}
1934
1935/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1936 * The RW stages of rw_opt in a RW step (see rw_triplet.h): the candidates are shortened (T_3 contraction, the rows of
1937 * G; rw_candidate()), the codewords of a step are recorded together at its end (lighter ones at once), each once per
1938 * step (rw_rec_t), and Stage 5 counts the canonical classes of the minimum weight found in the uniform steps, each at
1939 * most once per step (rw_canon_note_locked()).
1940 * ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ */
1941
1942/* The codewords found in the current RW step of a thread (rw_rec_buf): their sorted supports and keys (the first
1943 * `nflushed` of them recorded), and the canonical classes counted in this step */
1944typedef struct {
1945 int src; /* the kind of the step: CW_SRC_RW_UNIFORM, CW_SRC_RW_WINDOW, or CW_SRC_RW_SLAB */
1946 int nrec, cap; /* the codewords of the step (room for `cap`) */
1947 int nflushed; /* the codewords 0..nflushed-1 are recorded */
1948 int *off, *wt; /* their supports pool[off..off+wt-1] */
1949 uint32_t *spos; /* their slots */
1950 uint64_t *key; /* their Zobrist keys */
1951 uint64_t *ckey; /* their canonical keys (Stage 5; 0: not computed) */
1952 unsigned char *org; /* their origins (for steplog=FILE, see steplog_thr_t) */
1953 int *pool;
1954 size_t plen, pcap;
1955 int *slot; /* the hash of the keys: the codeword in each slot (-1: empty) */
1956 uint32_t smask;
1957 uint64_t *cset; /* the canonical keys counted in this step (open addressing, 0: empty) ... */
1958 uint32_t *cpos; /* ... in the slots cpos[0..ncset-1] */
1959 uint32_t cmask;
1960 int ncset;
1961} rw_rec_t;
1962
1963/* The state of the RW stages of a thread (see rw_thr_init()) */
1964typedef struct {
1965 rw_tws_t *ws; /* the workspace of the stages (rw_triplet.h) */
1966 rw_rec_t rec; /* the codewords of the current step */
1967 int *buf; /* a support of up to nvar + 2 columns (the shortened candidate) */
1968 int *cbuf; /* a support of up to nvar + 2 columns (the canonical form) */
1969 double *ltab; /* log(1 + s), s = 0..m, for the Harris-FKG score (see rw_pairs_step()) */
1970 /* Stage 3 (see rw_slab_step()) */
1971 word *S; /* the slab matrix: slab_msub rows of sw words */
1972 word *T; /* its transpose: the slab columns in the pivot rows */
1973 int *cols; /* the slab columns in their elimination order (columns of H) */
1974 int *spivs; /* the pivot column of each pivot row (slab columns) */
1975 word *spmask; /* the pivot columns (slab columns) */
1976 uint32_t *smark; /* the marks of the independent set of the triplet graph (generation sgen) */
1977 uint32_t sgen;
1978 int slab_r0, slab_r1; /* the detectors r0..r1-1 of the last slab (for steplog=FILE) */
1979 int slab_ns; /* and its columns */
1980} rw_thr_t;
1981
1982static void rec_init(rw_rec_t * const r) {
1983 memset(r, 0, sizeof(*r));
1984 r->cap = 64;
1985 r->off = malloc((size_t)r->cap * sizeof(int));
1986 r->wt = malloc((size_t)r->cap * sizeof(int));
1987 r->spos = malloc((size_t)r->cap * sizeof(uint32_t));
1988 r->key = malloc((size_t)r->cap * sizeof(uint64_t));
1989 r->ckey = malloc((size_t)r->cap * sizeof(uint64_t));
1990 r->org = malloc((size_t)r->cap);
1991 r->pcap = 1024;
1992 r->pool = malloc(r->pcap * sizeof(int));
1993 r->smask = 127;
